findings.issue_text: [High/bug] `OptimizedCursorPaginator` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `datetime` values when used with `order_by="-datetime"`, causing non-empty authorized `optimized_pagination=true` responses to raise `TypeError` while building a cursor; subsequent cursor values are also incompatible with the timestamp SQL filter.
[Medium/api] The negative-offset path slices a Django `QuerySet` with a negative start, which Django rejects; cursors such as `0:-1:0` can cause a 500 because only `BadPaginationError` is converted.

[High/data] Changing existing Redis payload keys from sets to sorted sets without migration or compatibility handling causes old/live keys or old-version writers during rollout to produce `WRONGTYPE` errors from `ZADD`/`ZCARD`/`ZSCAN`, interrupting span processing.
[Medium/data] `ZUNIONSTORE` uses its default `AGGREGATE SUM`, so replayed span payloads present in both source and destination have their end-time scores added together, corrupting eviction ordering.

[Medium/data] Eviction is hard-coded to 1,000 spans instead of respecting `self.max_segment_spans`, causing deployments with other configured limits to retain too many spans or discard permitted ones.
[Low/data] Reducing redirect traversal from 10,000 to 1,000 causes valid deeply nested segment trees with redirect chains over 1,000 to fail to join, producing fragmented segments.

goldens.comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/data] Changing existing Redis payload keys from sets to sorted sets without migration or compatibility handling causes old/live keys or old-version writers during rollout to produce `WRONGTYPE` errors from `ZADD`/`ZCARD`/`ZSCAN`, interrupting span processing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows changes in add-buffer.lua from set operations (scard, sunionstore, sadd) to sorted set operations (zcard, zunionstore, zadd). Similarly, buffer.py changes from sadd to zadd and sscan to zscan. During deployment rollout, if old code writes with SADD to a key and new code tries ZADD/ZCARD on the same key (or vice versa), Redis will return WRONGTYPE errors because sets and sorted sets are incompatible data types. The diff shows no migration strategy or compatibility handling for existing keys.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] `ZUNIONSTORE` uses its default `AGGREGATE SUM`, so replayed span payloads present in both source and destination have their end-time scores added together, corrupting eviction ordering.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ZUNIONSTORE being used in add-buffer.lua (lines like `span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)`). ZUNIONSTORE by default uses AGGREGATE SUM, meaning if the same span payload exists in both source sets, their scores (end_timestamp_precise values) will be added together rather than keeping one. This would corrupt the eviction ordering since zpopmin is used later to evict spans based on their scores. The finding correctly identifies that replayed/duplicate spans would have corrupted timestamps.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] Eviction is hard-coded to 1,000 spans instead of respecting `self.max_segment_spans`, causing deployments with other configured limits to retain too many spans or discard permitted ones.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in add-buffer.lua that the eviction limit is hard-coded to 1000 (`if span_count > 1000 then redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)`). Looking at buffer.py, there is a `self.max_segment_spans` attribute that was previously used for span count checking (the removed code shows `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans`). The Lua script should use a configurable limit passed as a parameter rather than hard-coding 1000, as this creates inconsistency with any configured `max_segment_spans` value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] Reducing redirect traversal from 10,000 to 1,000 causes valid deeply nested segment trees with redirect chains over 1,000 to fail to join, producing fragmented segments.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the loop limit being reduced from 10,000 to 1,000 in add-buffer.lua (line 30: 'for i = 0, 1000 do' replacing 'for i = 0, 10000 do'). The original comment explicitly stated 'theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly.' By reducing this to 1,000, any redirect chains between 1,000 and 10,000 deep will now fail to be properly traversed, causing segment trees to not join correctly. This is a real behavioral change that could cause data fragmentation for deeply nested traces.
